packages.name: neote-hello
packages.desc: A minimal demo package that toasts a greeting on enable and adds a clickable status-bar widget. Perfect first package to learn the Neote package API.
packages.author: neote
packages.markdown:
# neote-hello

`neote-hello` is the canonical "first package" for the Neote IDE. It demonstrates the three things every package should do:

1. **Register lifecycle hooks** with `neote.onEnable` / `neote.onDisable` so the IDE can start and stop you cleanly.
2. **Talk to the user** through `neote.toast` and `neote.log`.
3. **Own a piece of UI** through `neote.statusBar.add` and remove it again on disable.

## Install

```
neote install neote-hello
```

Or download `neote-hello.nep` from the package browser and open it in the IDE, then click **Install Package**.

## API used

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `neote.onEnable(fn)` | Called when the package is toggled on |
| `neote.onDisable(fn)` | Called when the package is toggled off |
| `neote.toast(msg, type)` | Show a transient toast (`info` / `success` / `error`) |
| `neote.log(msg, level)` | Write a line to the Main Terminal |
| `neote.statusBar.add({id, position, html, title, onclick})` | Add a status-bar widget |
| `neote.statusBar.remove(id)` | Remove a widget |
| `neote.pkg` | The parsed package metadata (`name`, `version`, ...) |

## License

MIT — use it as a template for your own packages.

packages.name: neote-clock
packages.desc: Adds a live, ticking clock to the right side of the Neote status bar. Updates every second and cleans up its interval timer on disable.
packages.author: neote
packages.markdown:
# neote-clock

A live clock that lives in the Neote IDE status bar. It ticks once per second and demonstrates the most important rule of Neote packages: **clean up after yourself on disable**.

## What it teaches

- Adding a widget with `neote.statusBar.add` to the `right` slot.
- Updating it in place with `neote.statusBar.update(id, html)` (no flicker, no duplicate widgets).
- Using `setInterval` and storing the handle on the package-scoped `neote` object so `onDisable` can clear it.

## Install

```
neote install neote-clock
```

## Behavior

| State | Status bar |
| --- | --- |
| Enabled | `🕐 14:32:07` (updates every second) |
| Disabled | widget removed, interval cleared |

## Notes

The `neote` object passed into your package is **instance-scoped** — every enabled package gets its own object, so storing timer handles on `neote._timer` is safe and won't collide with other packages.

## License

MIT

packages.name: neote-wordcount
packages.desc: Shows live word and character counts for the active editor in the status bar. Updates on every cursor move and content change.
packages.author: neote
packages.markdown:
# neote-wordcount

Live word and character counts for whatever file you're editing, shown in the status bar. It updates as you type **and** as you move the cursor.

## What it teaches

- Subscribing to editor events with `neote.editor.onCursor(fn)` and `neote.editor.onChange(fn)`.
- Each subscription returns an **unsubscribe function** that you must call in `onDisable`.
- Reading the editor buffer with `neote.editor.getValue()`.

## Install

```
neote install neote-wordcount
```

## Example output

```
align-left  42w / 318c
```

## API used

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `neote.editor.onCursor(fn)` | Fired on cursor movement; returns an unsub |
| `neote.editor.onChange(fn)` | Fired on content edits; returns an unsub |
| `neote.editor.getValue()` | Returns the current editor text |
| `neote.statusBar.add / update / remove` | Status-bar widget lifecycle |

## License

MIT

packages.name: neote-themes
packages.desc: Adds a clickable theme switcher to the status bar that cycles the IDE accent color through Purple, Ocean, Forest, Sunset and Rose. Also registers a theme.cycle terminal command.
packages.author: neote
packages.markdown:
# neote-themes

A theme switcher for the Neote IDE. Click the **palette** widget in the status bar — or run `theme.cycle()` in the terminal — to rotate the IDE accent through five palettes.

## Themes

| id | Name | Accent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `purple` | Purple | `#7c3aed` (default) |
| `ocean` | Ocean | `#0ea5e9` |
| `forest` | Forest | `#10b981` |
| `sunset` | Sunset | `#f59e0b` |
| `rose` | Rose | `#f43f5e` |

## What it teaches

- Making a **clickable** status-bar widget (`onclick`).
- Registering a **terminal command** with `neote.command.register(name, handler, desc)` and removing it with `neote.command.unregister(name)`.
- Driving the IDE look via a `data-neote-theme` attribute on `<html>` (the IDE ships CSS that recolors accent gradients for each value).

## Install

```
neote install neote-themes
```

## Usage

- **Status bar**: click the palette icon to cycle.
- **Terminal**: type `theme.cycle()` and press Enter.

The theme resets to Purple when the package is disabled.

## License

MIT

packages.name: neote-snippets
packages.desc: Registers terminal commands that insert common Neote DOM-loader snippets ($btn, $p, $hd, $input, $div, notify, showcase) at the cursor. Great for fast prototyping.
packages.author: neote
packages.markdown:
# neote-snippets

Speeds up writing `.neote` files by exposing snippet-inserting terminal commands. Type `snippet.btn()` in the terminal and the corresponding `$btn(...)` line is inserted at the editor cursor.

## Available commands

| Command | Inserts |
| --- | --- |
| `snippet.btn()` | `$btn("Click me") /id="btn1" /class="primary-btn"` |
| `snippet.p()` | `$p("Your paragraph text here.")` |
| `snippet.hd()` | `$hd("Section Title")` |
| `snippet.input()` | `$input("Placeholder text...") /id="inp1"` |
| `snippet.div()` | `$div("Container content") /class="box"` |
| `snippet.notify()` | `notify("Hello from Neote!")` |
| `snippet.showcase()` | `showcase("Logged value: " + value);` |

## What it teaches

- Registering **multiple** terminal commands in a loop (note the closure capture).
- Inserting text at the cursor with `neote.editor.insert(text)`.
- Tracking registered command names on the package scope so they can all be unregistered on disable.

## Install

```
neote install neote-snippets
```

## Tip

Combine with the IDE's autocomplete (Ctrl+Space) — snippets complement, they don't replace it.

## License

MIT
